summary: Iranian state media aired a presenter defending attacks on southern Iran with the phrase 'the south of Iran is sacrificed for the south of Lebanon,' sparking backlash online. Canada's Federal Court rejected a deportation stay for Salman Samani, a former Iranian Interior Ministry official, ordering his removal. Israeli airstrikes targeted a Hamas bomb site in northern Gaza overnight, with the IDF reporting no Israeli casualties.
key_points: Iranian state TV presenter said 'the south of Iran is sacrificed for the south of Lebanon' during coverage of airstrikes, drawing criticism online. (Source: @VahidOnline/77916)
Canada's Federal Court rejected Salman Samani's request to halt deportation; he must be removed after entering Canada on a tourist visa. (Source: @VahidOnline/77929)
IDF reported a Hamas bomb exploded near the Yellow Line in northern Gaza overnight, followed by gunfire; no Israeli injuries, and strikes were conducted afterward. (Source: @manniefabian/58982)
Israel and the US agreed to destroy Hamas weapons seized in Gaza under US supervision, with no reconstruction until full Hamas disarmament, per Israeli officials. (Source: @pkpoi/143629)

Iranian Majles approved a 33-article 'Countering Infiltration' bill restricting foreign academic ties, media contact, and cultural projects, with penalties including prison terms. (Source: @shin_persian/8990)
Israeli military sources said Netanyahu and Jared Kushner agreed no Gaza reconstruction begins before Hamas fully disarms, under US oversight. (Source: @Faytuks_Network/6353)
IDF conducted a military exercise in Judea and Samaria involving troop movements, vehicles, and aircraft, with explosions audible but no security threat. (Source: @idf_telegram/24917)

sections.executive_summary: Iranian state media defended airstrikes on southern Iran using inflammatory rhetoric, triggering domestic backlash. Canada's Federal Court ordered the deportation of a former Iranian Interior Ministry official. The IDF reported a Hamas attack near the Gaza-Israel border overnight, responding with airstrikes.

points: Iranian state TV presenter Reihaneh Qasemi-Zadeh stated 'the south of Iran is sacrificed for the south of Lebanon' while responding to criticism over airstrikes on southern Iran last month, framing critics as insincere sympathizers. (Source: @VahidOnline/77916)

The remarks sparked widespread condemnation across Iranian social media platforms, with many users expressing outrage over the perceived dismissal of civilian suffering in southern Iran, particularly in Bandar Abbas. (Source: @VahidOnline/77916)

Iran's Majles approved a 33-article 'Countering Infiltration' bill that imposes strict controls on foreign academic cooperation, media interactions, and cultural exchanges, with penalties including prison terms and professional bans. (Source: @shin_persian/8990)

MOIS will publish an annual whitelist of approved foreign entities for scholarships and scientific cooperation; unauthorized collaboration carries sentences of up to two years in prison. (Source: @shin_persian/8990)

The bill criminalizes sharing data with foreign media or individuals abroad, with harsher penalties during periods of unrest, and allows prosecutors to halt cultural projects deemed harmful to national interests. (Source: @shin_persian/8990)

A senior Iranian official told Reuters that Tehran has shifted from a defensive to an offensive posture, setting a deadline for full implementation of an understanding with the United States. (Source: @asafroz/52521)
The IDF reported a Hamas-planted bomb exploded on the Israeli side of the Yellow Line in northern Gaza overnight, followed by gunfire from Hamas operatives in the area. (Source: @manniefabrian/58982)

No Israeli forces were injured in the incident, and the IDF immediately conducted airstrikes against the site where the explosion and shooting occurred, labeling it a ceasefire violation. (Source: @manniefabian/58982)

Israeli officials told Channel 12 that Prime Minister Netanyahu and Jared Kushner agreed no Gaza reconstruction will begin until Hamas fully disarms, including light and heavy weapons, under US supervision. (Source: @Faytuks_Network/6353)
Israel will retain IDF freedom of action, including targeted strikes, and will not withdraw from the Yellow Line where security conditions require continued presence. (Source: @Faytuks_Network/6353)

A Knesset report indicated fewer Israelis are returning to occupied territories, citing ongoing conflict in Gaza, economic stagnation, and social pressures as contributing factors. (Source: @presstv/203196)

The IDF carried out a military exercise in Judea and Samaria involving significant troop, vehicle, and aircraft movements, with audible explosions reported but no security threat declared. (Source: @idf_telegram/24917)

The IDF reported a Hamas bomb detonated on the Israeli side of the Yellow Line in northern Gaza overnight, with Hamas operatives opening fire afterward in an area where an anti-Hamas militia is based. (Source: @manniefabian/58982)

Israel and the US agreed that Hamas weapons seized in Gaza will be transferred to US custody for destruction rather than handed over to the Palestinian Authority, as part of initial disarmament steps. (Source: @pkpoi/143629)

Israeli officials stated that Prime Minister Netanyahu and Jared Kushner agreed no Gaza reconstruction will begin before Hamas is fully disarmed, including both heavy and light weapons, under US supervision. (Source: @Faytuks_Network/6353)

A child victim of a stabbing incident in Beit Shemesh was confirmed dead; the two boys, aged 4 and 6, were not siblings but were staying with a 15-year-old relative suspected of carrying out the attack. (Source: @yediotnews25/134040)

Israeli National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir faced calls for EU sanctions after advocating killing 30 to 40 Gazans nightly, with critics labeling his remarks dehumanizing. (Source: @Faytuks_Network/6357)

Iranian state TV rhetoric linking southern Iran to southern Lebanon reflects broader regional tensions, with Hezbollah-aligned narratives gaining traction amid ongoing cross-border tensions. (Source: @VahidOnline/77916)

Unidentified military aircraft flew at medium altitude over southern Lebanon, raising concerns among local residents and security observers about potential escalation along the border. (Source: @rasedal3ado138e/385350)

The Israeli military reported intercepting a hostile target via radar systems operating in the southern sector, though no further details were provided regarding the nature or origin of the target. (Source: @naya_foriraq/88036)
Hezbollah-affiliated media reported Israeli reconnaissance flights over southern Lebanon, suggesting heightened surveillance activity amid ongoing regional instability. (Source: @redlinkleb/37111)

Israeli airstrikes targeted the runway of Abu al-Dhuhur military airport in eastern Idlib, where Turkish forces are reportedly stationed, according to regional sources. (Source: @rasedal3ado138e/385355)
A fuel tank exploded in Sulaymaniyah province in northern Iraq, causing a large fire but no immediate reports of casualties or injuries. (Source: @naya_foriraq/88030)

Iraqi political figures criticized government handling of security affairs, calling for corrections to policies they claim have destabilized the country and undermined national dignity. (Source: @naya_foriraq/88025)
Iranian-backed groups in Iraq continue to voice support for resistance operations, though specific actions remain unreported in recent communications. (Source: @naya_foriraq/88017)
Jordan's King Abdullah II is scheduled to visit China tomorrow, according to the Chinese Foreign Ministry, marking a diplomatic engagement amid shifting regional alliances. (Source: @asafroz/52513)

Germany experienced a cyberattack targeting two federal ministries in Berlin's state government, highlighting growing concerns over digital infrastructure vulnerabilities in European capitals. (Source: @naya_foriraq/88017)

Gulf Cooperation Council states have not issued formal statements regarding recent developments in Gaza or Iran, maintaining a low-profile stance amid ongoing regional tensions. (Source: @presstv/203194)

sections.threat_assessment: Regional tensions remain high with active exchanges between Israeli and Palestinian factions along the Gaza border, including a recent Hamas bomb attack near the Yellow Line. Iranian rhetoric linking southern Iran to Lebanon signals potential for broader escalation, while new legislation tightening domestic control suggests internal instability. Cross-border incidents in Lebanon and Syria, including Israeli airstrikes and reconnaissance flights, indicate a volatile environment prone to rapid deterioration.
sections.regional_response: International actors have responded cautiously to recent developments. Canada enforced the deportation of a former Iranian official, while European lawmakers called for sanctions against Israeli ministers over inflammatory statements. Diplomatic engagements, such as Jordan's upcoming visit to China, suggest efforts to balance regional pressures through strategic partnerships.
sections.intelligence_notes: Iranian domestic policy appears focused on consolidating control through restrictive legislation, potentially limiting external influence and dissent. Israeli military readiness is evident through exercises and rapid response to border incidents, indicating preparedness for sustained operations. Cyber threats and physical attacks across multiple theaters underscore the complexity of monitoring non-state actors in the region.
